chunks: On this same day, after the gathering, the virtuous scholar Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Abdullah b. al-Hasan al-Muaddib narrated to us from Ahmad b. Ali al-Isfahani, from Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Thaqafi, who said: Abu Ghassan al-Nahdi narrated to us, saying: Yahya b. Salamah b. Kuhayl narrated to us from his father, from Abu Idris, from al-Musayyib b. Najabah, from Ali (peace be upon him)

that it was said to him: Tell us about the companions of Muhammad (may Allah bless him and his family). Tell us about Abu Dharr al-Ghifari. He said: He learned knowledge and then sealed it, binding it with a tight seal. They said: What about Hudhayfah? He said: He learned the names of the hypocrites. They said: What about Ammar b. Yasir? He said: A believer filled to his very core with faith; he forgets, but when reminded, he remembers. It was said: What about Abdullah b. Mas'ud? He said: He recited the Quran, and it descended upon him. They said: Tell us about Salman al-Farisi. He said: He attained the knowledge of the first and the last, and he is an ocean that cannot be emptied, and he is from us, the Ahl al-Bayt. They said: Then tell us about yourself, O Commander of the Believers. He said: I was such that when I asked, I was given, and when I was silent, I was initiated.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Believers — title of Imam Ali (AS)
key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt — the People of the House, referring to the Prophet's household
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقِينَ: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess Islam but secretly disbelieve

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the companions Abu Dharr, Hudhayfah, Ammar, Ibn Mas'ud, and Salman al-Farisi?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) provides succinct character portraits of five prominent companions of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) when asked about them by his followers. He describes Abu Dharr as a guardian of sealed knowledge, Hudhayfah as the keeper of hypocrites' names, Ammar ibn Yasir as a faithful believer, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud as a recipient of Quranic revelation, and Salman al-Farisi as possessing both ancient and latter knowledge and being counted among the Ahl al-Bayt. When asked about himself, Ali (AS) modestly states that he received answers when he asked and was proactively taught when he remained silent.
